previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 78-year-old male with a history of severe aortic stenosis, diastolic heart failure, atrial fibrillation, and chronic bronchitis was admitted for right leg swelling, erythema, and pain that began one week prior. He had been treated for presumed dermatitis without improvement. Evaluation ruled out DVT, and he was diagnosed with cellulitis and stasis dermatitis. He also had signs of pulmonary edema due to decompensated diastolic heart failure, confirmed by chest X-ray and echocardiogram. He was treated with IV vancomycin and ciprofloxacin, later transitioned to oral cephalexin and sulfamethoxazole-trimethoprim. Diuresis with furosemide improved his respiratory status and leg swelling. His anemia remained stable, and he was discharged home with home health services, oral antibiotics, and instructions to monitor weight and symptoms. He was advised to follow up with his primary care physician.
problems: Cellulitis and abscess of leg, except foot

pneumonia or effusion.

FINDINGS:  Frontal and lateral chest radiographs again demonstrate enlargement
of the cardiac silhouette.  Cardiomediastinal contour is otherwise unchanged
and calcifications in the aortic arch are noted.  Small to moderate right
pleural effusion  has slightly increased. Small left pleural effusion is
stable. Fluid is again seen within the minor fissure. Increased opacification
at the right base could relate to increased effusion and mild pulmonary edema;
but consolidation is not excluded. There is no pneumothorax.  Extensive
degenerative changes of both glenohumeral joints and clavicles are again seen.

HISTORY:  ___ male with worsening dyspnea in the setting of congestive
heart failure.  

TECHNIQUE:  Single frontal chest radiograph was obtained portably with the
patient in an upright position.

COMPARISON:  ___.  

FINDINGS:

There has been interval redistribution of the moderate-sized right pleural
effusion, which now layers dependently rather than in the fissure. Small left
pleural effusion has increased.  Bibasilar consolidations most likely
represent atelectasis, but pneumonia cannot be excluded.  Heart size is
enlarged.  Aortic calcification is seen.  Mediastinal contours are otherwise
within normal limits.  No pneumothorax is detected.  Mild interstitial edema
may be slightly improved.  Degenerative change of the left glenohumeral joint
is partially imaged.  

IMPRESSION:

Redistributed moderate right pleural effusion and increased small left pleural
effusion.  Minimally improved interstitial edema.  Bibasilar consolidations
most likely represent atelectasis, but pneumonia cannot be excluded.
